answer: Like rainwater carving through porous karst, trust in our consensus protocol cannot be fabricated overnight. Every agent anchors to a verifiable social-computational harbor, where subjective graph flow weights peer validation. When an attacker attempts to spawn clone identities, transitive verification distances trigger a steep cost spiral: the capital required scales with superlinear staking requirements ($O(N^2)$), starving counterfeit nodes before they can establish legitimacy across the topology.
